To determine the weight of the Mastiff, we will calculate the weight of each dog in the line sequentially based on the relationships provided in the problem statement.

**Step 1: Weight of the Affenpinscher**
The problem states that the first dog, the Affenpinscher, weighed 10 pounds.
$$ W_{\text{Affenpinscher}} = 10 \text{ lbs} $$

**Step 2: Weight of the Dachshund**
The Dachshund sat next to the Affenpinscher and weighed twice as much as the Affenpinscher.
$$ W_{\text{Dachshund}} = 2 \times W_{\text{Affenpinscher}} $$
$$ W_{\text{Dachshund}} = 2 \times 10 = 20 \text{ lbs} $$

**Step 3: Weight of the Papillon**
The Papillon sat next to the Dachshund and weighed one-fourth as much as the Dachshund.
$$ W_{\text{Papillon}} = \frac{1}{4} \times W_{\text{Dachshund}} $$
$$ W_{\text{Papillon}} = \frac{1}{4} \times 20 = 5 \text{ lbs} $$

**Step 4: Weight of the Mastiff**
The Mastiff sat at the end of the line and weighed 44 times the weight of the Papillon.
$$ W_{\text{Mastiff}} = 44 \times W_{\text{Papillon}} $$
$$ W_{\text{Mastiff}} = 44 \times 5 $$

Calculating the product:
$$ 44 \times 5 = 220 $$
